issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt breaks or loosens
issues.sym: Power steering suddenly goes heavy, warning lights come on, the battery stops charging, or the A/C quits. You may hear a wobble or knock from the front of the engine, and belts can come off.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley can loosen or snap, letting the pulley wobble or fall off so it no longer drives the belts. RepairPal lists it as the most common Montero problem, and some owners report it coming back after a repair.
issues.next: If steering goes heavy and lights come on at once, pull over safely. Have the pulley and bolt replaced with new parts torqued to spec, and have the crankshaft nose checked for damage.

issues.sym: A wobbling crank pulley, belt noise, or loss of power steering and charging.
issues.why: On 1996 Monteros with the 3.0L V6, the crank pulley bolt could loosen and let the pulley fall off. Dealers tighten the bolt to spec and replace damaged bolts.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer whether recall 00V311001 was done on your truck.

issues.sym: A loud buzzing or chirping noise from under the hood, the ABS or brake light coming on, a hard pedal, or lost power assist so the truck is hard to stop.
issues.why: These Monteros use an electric-hydraulic brake booster instead of a vacuum one. Its pump, accumulator or control parts wear out, and owners report loss of assist at higher mileage.
issues.next: Treat a hard pedal or brake light as urgent and have the brake booster system diagnosed. Don't drive it if the pedal is hard or sinks.

issues.t: Brake booster accumulator can leak gas (recall)
issues.sym: A noise when braking, and the first brake press after the truck has been parked may get little or no power assist.
issues.why: The nitrogen-filled accumulator on the hydraulic brake booster could be built wrong and slowly leak. Dealers install an improved accumulator. Some owners report their VIN was left out of the recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 01V254001. If you have these symptoms and the recall doesn't apply, get the booster checked anyway.

issues.sym: Slow or delayed shifts, the engine flaring between gears, slipping in 2nd or 3rd, or the transmission dropping into neutral and not engaging.
issues.why: Transmission shifting faults are the top reported 2001 Montero problem, averaging about 119,000 miles. Fluid leaks and internal wear are suspected causes.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Have the transmission codes read and the fluid serviced before damage gets worse.

issues.t: Horn sounds by itself, especially in cold weather
issues.sym: The horn honks on its own when it gets cold, when the wheel is turned or in the middle of the night, sometimes running the battery down.
issues.why: A worn contact inside the steering wheel horn pad can short. Many owners pull the horn fuse to stop it.
issues.next: Have the horn switch in the steering wheel inspected. Don't leave the horn fuse out longer than needed since you lose the horn.

issues.sym: Heavy rust or holes on the frame, wheel wells or underbody. In bad cases the frame cracks.
issues.why: Owners report frame rot and fractures on these trucks, especially in road-salt areas, past 90,000 miles or so.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift, especially before buying. Severe frame rust can make the truck unsafe to drive.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve can leak when parked uphill (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell or fuel dripping near the tank after filling up and parking nose-up on a warm day.
issues.why: The fuel tank leveling valve might not seal when a full tank expands in the heat. Dealers replace the valve.
issues.next: Avoid parking uphill on a full tank. Ask a dealer to check recall 04V319000.

issues.t: Fuel leaking from the tank area or pump hoses
issues.sym: A raw gas smell or fuel dripping from under the rear of the truck.
issues.why: Owners report fuel leaking from the hoses at the fuel pump, the fill pipe and rusted parts of the tank.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Have the tank, pump hoses and filler neck inspected right away.

issues.sym: No warning signs. In a crash the driver airbag could rupture or not inflate correctly.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator can absorb moisture over time, which may cause it to burst or underinflate. Mitsubishi replaces the inflator for free.
issues.next: Have a Mitsubishi dealer check recall 20V035000 right away.

issues.t: Third-row seat may not latch because of cargo mat (recall)
issues.sym: The folded third-row seat doesn't latch firmly.
issues.why: The accessory cargo mat could get in the way of the third-row seat latches. Dealers trim the mat around the strikers.
issues.next: Make sure the third-row seats latch firmly. Ask a dealer to confirm recall 98V205000.

issues.t: Front brake lines can chafe through (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on, the pedal feels low, or brake fluid leaks near the front wheels.
issues.why: The front brake lines could rub against the edge of a hole in the inner fender until they wore pinholes. Dealers reposition or replace them.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 98V220000 and inspect the front brake lines.

issues.t: Passenger mirror doesn't give a wide enough view (recall)
issues.sym: Limited view out of the passenger-side mirror.
issues.why: Some passenger-side mirrors didn't meet the federal visibility standard. Dealers replace the mirror.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether recall 00V123002 applies.

issues.t: Front-end vibration and worn steering parts
issues.sym: Shaking or shimmy in the steering wheel at highway speeds, the truck pulling to one side, loose steering or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Worn front suspension and steering parts, such as tie rods, ball joints, bushings and wheel bearings, are a commonly reported Montero problem.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and worn parts replaced, then get an alignment.

issues.t: 4WD, transfer case or ABS lights flashing
issues.sym: The 4WD indicator and ABS lights flash, the transfer case warning light comes back on, or the drive mode gets stuck in AWD.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the transfer case shift system and ABS sensors that set these warning lights.
issues.next: Have the codes read for both the ABS and the 4WD system. Avoid shifting modes repeatedly until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Oil burning from leaking valve guides
issues.sym: Blue smoke from the exhaust, especially at startup, and oil disappearing between changes.
issues.why: The 3.5L and 3.8L V6 engines in these Monteros are known for leaking valve guides, which let oil into the cylinders.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. Have a compression and leak-down test done if smoke or oil use gets worse.

issues.t: Timing belt, tensioner or idler failure
issues.sym: A chattering or whining noise from the front of the engine, or the engine suddenly quitting and not restarting.
issues.why: These V6 engines use a timing belt, and the 3.5L and 3.8L are interference engines, so a broken belt can bend valves. Owners report noisy tensioners and idlers.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt, tensioner and idler on schedule. Many owners use about 60,000 miles. Don't put off a belt-area noise.

issues.t: Stalling at speed or when accelerating
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving at highway speed, at low RPM or pulling away from a stop.
issues.why: Several owners report stalling on these years. The cause varies, so stored codes are the best clue.
issues.next: Have the codes read right after a stall and avoid highway driving until it is found.

issues.t: Warped rotors and fast brake pad wear
issues.sym: Pulsing brake pedal, grinding or squealing, or pads that wear out early.
issues.why: Owners report the heavy truck wearing pads and warping rotors quickly.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Use quality pads and rotors and replace them as a set.
